A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations of the proposed algorithms on PetShop, Sock-shop, and ProRCA in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original synthetic, real-world, and semi-synthetic evaluations, including numerical results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: SMOOTH TRAVERSAL and SCORE ORDERING retain the same anomaly scores, inputs, selection rules, and pseudocode in Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic SCM settings, PetShop traffic scenarios, Sock-shop fault types, and four ProRCA anomaly scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: Cholesky, Traversal, Circa, Counterfactual, RCD, and epsilon-Diagnosis, together with the additional PetShop comparators. New statistical citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain the same data generation, model configurations, sample counts, recall metrics, and tie handling. The distinction between single-anomaly-sample evaluations and the larger samples supplied to RCD and epsilon-Diagnosis is unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing anomaly-strength, graph-size, linearity, polytree, graph-misspecification, and tied-score analyses are retained. Repositioned passages and figures in Appendix F do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain 100 repetitions per synthetic data point, 100 replicates per ProRCA anomaly type, the same runtime boxplots, and the same uncertainty-reporting disclosures. The expanded theoretical proof does not change experimental statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The experimental graphics and numerical entries in Tables 1–10 are unchanged. For example, Table 10 reports SCORE ORDERING recall of 0.94 for FulfillmentSpike and 0.00 for ReturnSurge in both versions.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 replaces v3's reference to an external proof with an explicit Erlang-distribution and probability-integral-transform proof of Lemma 3.8. Appendix C.1 also corrects the union-bound reference from equations 24 and 25 to 24 and 26. The theorem statements and bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about RCA from marginal anomaly scores, guarantees under the stated assumptions, and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning polytrees, applicability beyond polytrees, linearity, tied anomaly scores, and dataset-specific failures remain unchanged in Section 3.5 and Appendices E–F.

D1.justification: Section 4 changes the code address from worchard/rca-with-missing-structural-knowledge to amazon-science/RCAWithMissingStructuralKnowledgeCode. Other implementation, parameter, and hardware disclosures are retained; the PDFs do not establish changes to the repository contents.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Tippett (1931) and Ibe (2013), connects Theorem 3.12 to Tippett's method, and explicitly identifies the existing joint-score construction with Fisher's method. These are limited additions to statistical attribution.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited wording edits in Section 4, expands proof exposition and statistical footnotes, and adds funding acknowledgments for Peterhouse and Cancer Research UK. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their designs and numbering, but their placement and surrounding page breaks change. Figure 4 moves from page 30 to 31, Figure 6 from page 31 to 32, and Table 10 from page 37 to 38.

improvement.justification: The self-contained proof in Appendix C.4 makes the joint-score calibration easier to verify, while the corrected union-bound reference and clearer statistical attribution improve precision. These limited gains outweigh the less compact appendix layout; the methods, empirical evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
